errorRules.message: GradientAI rejected the credential (HTTP 401, "Unable to authenticate you"). Check {apiKeyEnvVar}. Model access keys are created at {setupUrl}
GradientAI API rate limit exceeded (HTTP 429; the Serverless Inference API reference documents the 429 body as "API rate limit exceeded.")

GradientAI returned 404 "Model not found" for '{model}'. The Model Support Policy page (docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/model-support-policy) states that requests to deprecated model IDs return this error.

instructions: 1. Visit: https://cloud.digitalocean.com/model-studio/manage-keys (the Control Panel page that https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/how-to/manage-model-access-keys/ names for creating and managing model access keys; it shows the DigitalOcean login when signed out) and sign in to a DigitalOcean account
2. Click Create model access key, enter a name, and copy the secret key when it is shown: the docs state "Copy and store it securely before closing the window."

3. Prepaid balance: the docs state "Serverless Inference requires a positive prepaid account balance before you can send inference requests." (https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/how-to/manage-serverless-inference-prepayment/)
setup.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://inference.do-ai.run/v1 (the models page says the text models are "served through OpenAI-compatible endpoints", and the Chat Completions page's Python OpenAI SDK example sets base_url="https://inference.do-ai.run/v1"). Docs-verified only: GET https://inference.do-ai.run/v1/models answers 401 without a key, so the 12 chat model ids come from the vendor's models page and the roster has not been checked. models.defaultContextWindow (32,768) and models.defaultMaxOutputTokens (4,096) are placeholders the vendor does not publish. The unauthenticated GET of /v1/models returned the body {"id": "Unauthorized", "message": "Unable to authenticate you" }; the API reference documents 401, 429 and 500 responses for chat completions, and errorRules covers 401, 429 and the 404 "Model not found" response described on the Model Support Policy page.
